Microsoft
Copilot Cowork Enablement Camp • Lab 2

🧩 Build the Northwind Cowork Plugin

Connect the Northwind Traders sample database to Cowork using an MCP server, Microsoft Dev Tunnels, WIQD, a connector, and a custom skill.

Beginner friendlyWindows PowerShell (Admin)WIQDMCP + Dev Tunnels
Lab flow: Prerequisites → Terminal 1 (database + MCP server) → Terminal 2 (Dev Tunnel) → Terminal 3 (build plugin) → Cowork (test)

Setup

⚙️ Prerequisites

Prepare your machine. Install or verify every tool before starting the lab.

1

Open PowerShell as Administrator

All commands in this lab run from PowerShell. Administrator mode avoids permission issues while installing tools and creating folders.

  1. Select Start and type PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as administrator.
  3. Select Yes in the User Account Control prompt.
What to expect: A PowerShell window opens with Administrator in the title bar.
2

Check PowerShell version (7 or later)

WIQD requires PowerShell version 7 or later. Older Windows PowerShell (5.1) can cause commands to fail.

Check that your PowerShell version is 7 or later:

PowerShell
pwsh --version
What to expect: The output shows PowerShell 7.x.x.

If pwsh is not recognized, install the latest PowerShell (version 7 or later):

PowerShell
winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget

After installation, search for PowerShell from Start and run the check again:

PowerShell
pwsh --version
Important: The version check is only needed here. For the remaining lab steps, open Windows PowerShell from Start and use Run as administrator.
3

Check Node.js and npm

Node.js runs the MCP server (supergateway and mcp-sqlite) through npx.

PowerShell
node --version
PowerShell
npm --version
What to expect: Both commands return a version number (your version may be newer).

If either command is not recognized, install Node.js LTS, then close and reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e
4

Check Work IQ Dev Tools (WIQD)

WIQD creates, configures, provisions, and packages the Cowork plugin.

PowerShell
wiqd --version
What to expect: A version number is returned.

If WIQD is not recognized, install it, then reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
iex "& { $(irm 'https://aka.ms/wiqd/install.ps1') }"
5

Check the Microsoft Dev Tunnels CLI

Dev Tunnels gives your local MCP server a public HTTPS URL so Cowork can reach it.

PowerShell
devtunnel --version
What to expect: The output shows Tunnel CLI version and the tunnel service details.

If devtunnel is not recognized, install it, then reopen Windows PowerShell as Administrator:

PowerShell
winget install --id Microsoft.devtunnel -e
Terminal 1

🗄️ Terminal 1 — Northwind database & MCP server

Download the Northwind database and start the MCP server. This terminal stays open until the end of the lab.

6

Use your Administrator Windows PowerShell window as Terminal 1

Terminal 1 will host the MCP server that connects to the Northwind database.

Use the Windows PowerShell Administrator window from the prerequisites. If you closed it, open a new one:

  1. Select Start and search for Windows PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as administrator.
  3. Select Yes in the User Account Control prompt.
What to expect: One Windows PowerShell window open with Administrator in the title bar. This is Terminal 1.
7

Create the lab folder

This folder holds the Northwind database and the plugin project.

PowerShell
mkdir C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab
View reference output
PowerShell
cd C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab
View reference output
What to expect: Your prompt shows PS C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab>.
8

Download the Northwind database

Northwind Traders is a sample company database with customers, orders, products, and suppliers. This is the data your plugin will query.

PowerShell
curl.exe -L -o northwind.db https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpwhite3/northwind-SQLite3/main/dist/northwind.db
View reference output
What to expect: The progress reaches 100% and northwind.db (about 23 MB) is saved in the lab folder.
9

Start the Northwind MCP server

mcp-sqlite exposes the database as MCP tools (list tables, describe table, read and write queries). supergateway makes those tools available over HTTP on port 3000.

PowerShell
npx -y supergateway --stdio "npx -y mcp-sqlite ./northwind.db" --outputTransport streamableHttp --port 3000
View reference output
What to expect: You see Listening on port 3000 and StreamableHttp endpoint: http://localhost:3000/mcp.
Keep Terminal 1 open. Do not close it or press Ctrl+C. If it stops, the plugin cannot reach the database.
Terminal 2

🌐 Terminal 2 — Microsoft Dev Tunnel

Publish the MCP server on a public HTTPS URL. Keep Terminal 1 running.

10

Open a second Windows PowerShell as Administrator

The MCP server occupies Terminal 1, so the tunnel needs its own window.

Leave Terminal 1 running, and open another window:

  1. Select Start and search for Windows PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as administrator.
  3. Select Yes in the User Account Control prompt.
What to expect: You now have two Windows PowerShell windows. Terminal 2 is used only for Dev Tunnels.
11

Sign in to Dev Tunnels

Dev Tunnels requires a signed-in user before it can host a tunnel.

PowerShell
devtunnel user login
What to expect: A browser sign-in window opens. Sign in with your account. PowerShell confirms you are logged in.
12

Host the tunnel on port 3000

This publishes your local port 3000 to a public HTTPS URL that Cowork can call.

PowerShell
devtunnel host -p 3000 --allow-anonymous
View reference output
What to expect: The output shows Connect via browser URLs and ends with Ready to accept connections.
Copy your lab URL. Use the URL in this format (yours will be different):
https://93sn4kwg-3000.inc1.devtunnels.ms
Keep Terminal 2 open. Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 must stay running for the rest of the lab.
Terminal 3

🛠️ Terminal 3 — Build the plugin with WIQD

Create, configure, provision, and package the Cowork plugin. Keep Terminals 1 and 2 running.

13

Open a third Windows PowerShell as Administrator

Terminal 3 is used to build the plugin with WIQD.

Open one more window:

  1. Select Start and search for Windows PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell and select Run as administrator.
  3. Select Yes in the User Account Control prompt.

Then go to the lab folder:

PowerShell
cd C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab
View reference output
What to expect: Three Windows PowerShell windows are open. All remaining commands run in Terminal 3.
14

Create the plugin project

WIQD generates the plugin structure, including manifest.json and the lifecycle files needed for provisioning.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin create --name northwind-cowork-plugin
View reference output
PowerShell
cd C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab\northwind-cowork-plugin
View reference output
What to expect: A northwind-cowork-plugin folder is created, containing an appPackage folder, and your prompt is inside the project.
15

Create toolDescription.json in Notepad

This file tells Cowork which MCP tools exist and what inputs each tool needs.

  1. Open Notepad.
  2. Copy the JSON below and paste it into Notepad.
  3. Select File > Save As.
  4. Browse to C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab\northwind-cowork-plugin\appPackage.
  5. Set Save as type to All files (*.*).
  6. Enter the file name toolDescription.json and select Save.
JSON
{
  "name": "Northwind Traders DB",
  "description": "Query and update Northwind Traders customers, orders, and inventory records.",
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "list_tables",
      "description": "List all tables in the Northwind database.",
      "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {} }
    },
    {
      "name": "describe_table",
      "description": "Get column names and schema details for a table in Northwind.",
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "table_name": { "type": "string", "description": "Name of the Northwind table to describe." }
        },
        "required": [ "table_name" ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "read_query",
      "description": "Execute a SELECT SQL query to pull records from Northwind.",
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "query": { "type": "string", "description": "The SELECT SQL query to execute." }
        },
        "required": [ "query" ]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "write_query",
      "description": "Execute an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE SQL query to update Northwind records.",
      "inputSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "query": { "type": "string", "description": "The INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE SQL query to execute." }
        },
        "required": [ "query" ]
      }
    }
  ]
}
View reference output
What to expect: toolDescription.json appears in the appPackage folder (not toolDescription.json.txt).
16

Add the Northwind MCP connector

The connector links the plugin to your MCP server through the tunnel URL.

Replace <YOUR-LAB-URL> with the Dev Tunnel URL you copied in Terminal 2. Keep /mcp at the end with no space before it.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin add connector --name "NorthWindDB" --description "Northwind Traders Order Management Database" --url "<YOUR-LAB-URL>/mcp" --tool-description ./toolDescription.json
Example URL: https://93sn4kwg-3000.inc1.devtunnels.ms/mcp
View reference output
What to expect: WIQD confirms the connector was added to the plugin manifest.
17

Add the order-manager skill

A skill gives Cowork instructions on how and when to use the connector tools.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin add skill --name "order-manager"
View reference output

Now edit the skill instructions in Notepad:

  1. Open C:\Northwind-Cowork-Lab\northwind-cowork-plugin\appPackage\skills\order-manager\SKILL.md in Notepad.
  2. Select all existing content and delete it.
  3. Copy the Markdown below, paste it, and select File > Save.
Markdown
---
name: order-manager
description: Query and update customer orders in Northwind Traders.
---

When the user asks about orders or customers:
- Always run list_tables and describe_table first if you are unsure of exact column names.
- Use read_query to fetch matching records and present them in a clean markdown table.
- When asked to update or ship an order, execute write_query with a targeted UPDATE statement and verify the change with a follow-up read_query.
What to expect: SKILL.md contains only the order-manager instructions above.
18

Sign in to WIQD

Provisioning uploads the plugin to Microsoft 365, so WIQD needs your work account.

PowerShell
wiqd auth login --interactive
View reference output
What to expect: After you sign in with the lab account that has Cowork access, WIQD confirms the sign-in.
19

Provision the plugin

Provisioning registers the plugin in your tenant and generates its app ID.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin provision --env dev
View reference output
What to expect: Provisioning completes without errors.
Continue only after provisioning succeeds. Packaging depends on it.
20

Package the plugin

Packaging builds the final plugin ZIP that Cowork installs.

PowerShell
wiqd plugin package --env dev
View reference output
What to expect: WIQD creates the plugin package and reports no validation errors.
Please wait 2–3 minutes. After packaging/provisioning, the new plugin can take a few minutes to appear in Cowork before you continue to the next section.
Cowork

🚀 Cowork — Enable and test the plugin

Open the plugin in Cowork and run a test prompt. Keep Terminals 1 and 2 running.

21

Open the plugin in Cowork

Cowork loads plugins you have provisioned. Here you confirm it arrived with its connector and skill.

  1. Sign in to Cowork with your lab account.
  2. Select Plugins in the left navigation.
View reference output

Find the plugin you deployed and select it to open its details.

View reference output
What to expect: The plugin details page lists the NorthWindDB connector and the order-manager skill. Turn the plugin on if it is not already enabled.
22

Test the plugin in Cowork

This confirms the full chain works: Cowork → plugin → connector → Dev Tunnel → MCP server → Northwind database.

Start a new Cowork conversation and enter this prompt:

Prompt
Using Northwind DB list the 5 unshipped orders along with their order id, customer id and freight cost
View reference output

Cowork first checks the database structure. When asked, approve the tool request so it can read the table schema.

View reference output

Cowork then generates a read-only SELECT query. Review it and approve it.

View reference output

Cowork runs the query through your MCP server and returns the results.

View reference output
What to expect: A table of five unshipped orders with Order ID, Customer ID, and freight cost. You can also see the requests arrive in Terminal 1.
🎉
Great, you finished connecting the plugin!
Your Northwind database now answers questions in Cowork through MCP, Dev Tunnels, a connector, and a custom skill.
Northwind Cowork Plugin Lab • Keep Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 open until you finish testing.
